description: Galbi, a beloved Korean BBQ classic, features succulent beef short ribs marinated in a sweet and savory sauce, then grilled to perfection. This iconic dish offers an irresistible blend of tender meat and rich flavors, making it a centerpiece for any gathering. Prepare to impress with this authentic and easy-to-follow Galbi recipe.

instructions.title: Prepare the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Rinse the Flanken-cut short ribs under cold water to remove any bone fragments or impurities. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. You can lightly score the ribs on both sides if desired to help the marinade penetrate deeper, but it is not strictly necessary for this cut.

instructions.title: Make the Galbi Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated Asian pear, grated yellow onion, minced garlic, grated fresh ginger, sesame oil, mirin (if using), and black pepper. Whisk all ingredients together until the sugar is fully dissolved and the marinade is well combined. The pear and onion will act as natural tenderizers and add a subtle sweetness.

instructions.title: Marinate the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Add the prepared short ribs to the marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. You can use a large resealable plastic bag or a non-reactive container. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor and tenderization. Longer marinating times (up to 24 hours) will yield more flavorful results.

instructions.title: Preheat Grill or Pan
instructions.text: When ready to cook, preheat your grill to medium-high heat (about 375-400°F or 190-200°C). If using a cast-iron griddle or heavy-bottomed pan, preheat it over medium-high heat until hot. Lightly brush the grill grates or pan with a little oil to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Galbi
instructions.text: Remove the short ribs from the marinade, allowing any excess to drip off. Discard the remaining marinade. Place the ribs on the preheated grill or pan. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. The ribs should have beautiful char marks and be cooked through but still juicy and tender. Avoid overcooking to prevent dryness.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, transfer the Galbi to a cutting board or platter. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist ribs. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions. Serve immediately with rice and banchan.

tips: For extra tender Galbi, ensure you use a fresh Asian pear in your marinade; its enzymes naturally break down tough meat fibers.
If you cant find Flanken-cut ribs, you can use bone-in English cut short ribs and butterfly them, or use boneless short ribs, adjusting cooking time.
Always let your Galbi rest for a few minutes after grilling. This crucial step helps redistribute the juices, resulting in a more tender and flavorful bite.
